mount-encrypted: add the new cmdline option "insecure" mount-encrypted doesn't store an insecure system key in NVRAM, which allows us to keep encstateful not wiped over TPM clearing and avoids potential unexpected behavior caused by soft-clearing TPM 2.0. The option should only be enabled for testing purposes and will be used in the autotest env. This CL provdes an alternative and simpler way to solve the soft-clearing TPM 2.0 problem mentioned above, compared with the original solution in CL:1753389. BUG=b:139399088 TEST=tested along with CL:1763468: On a chell, make sure the changes are no-op in any case. On a soraka, create the magic file in /mnt/stateful_partition, then 1. Run crossystem to clear the TPM, reboot, and log in. Then, repeat those 3 steps a few times and make sure each time the encrypted partition is not wiped. Also, check if mount-encrypted.log says it uses an insecure system key. 2. Run tpm_softclear to soft-clear the TPM, then run tpm_manager_client take_ownership to re-own the TPM, then reboot. Make sure the encrypted partition isn't wiped and mount-encrypted.log says it uses an insecure system key. 3. Remove the magic file, run crossystem to clear the TPM, reboot, and make sure the encrypted partition is wiped and mount-encrypted.log says it creates a random key and stores it in NVRAM. Change-Id: I68c762de6115ec33e3ea7ebc35f50f7264578b21 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1763467 Tested-by: Wei-Cheng Xiao <garryxiao@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: ChromeOS CL Exonerator Bot <chromiumos-cl-exonerator@appspot.gserviceaccount.com> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mattias Nissler <mnissler@chromium.org>

power: use event_count instead of wakeup_count event_count increments for a given device when pm_wakeup_event() is called by the associated driver. wakeup_count on the other hand increments only for the first device that reported the wake when in suspend/resume path. This is a problem in couple of scenarios: 1. When a wake is triggered by USB hid, wakeup count might only increments for root hub controller and not for the actual hid. 2. When a wake is triggered by a mfd device, only the mfd device wakeup count might increment and the sub-platform device's (enumerated by mfd devices) wakeup count might not increment. This change thus changes powerd code to depend on event_count rather than wakeup_count. Please look at https://lore.kernel.org/linux-pm/20190619175142.237794-1-ravisadineni@chromium.org/ for more info on why wakeup_count is not a reliable. BUG=b:133262012, b:65976859 TEST=Deploy on nocturne on test dark and full wake sources. shill: Connection: Remove Request/ReleaseRouting This patch prepares te removal of Connection from PortalDetector and HttopRequest. Calls to Connection::RequestRouting and ::ReleaseRouting are moved from HttpRequest to Device. Since the latter knows when a full multi probe trial is finished, it can call RequestRouting and ReleaseRouting exactly once, which remove the need for ref counting the number of RequestRouting calls. Since there is no other user of these two methods, they are also removed from Connection. pytests/wireless_radiotap: make Intel-specific config optional The 'bf_params' file is Intel-specific and should not cause a non-Intel-WiFi device to fail the test. It appears to be useful for helping ensure (more-)reliable monitor-mode capture of beacons, and so removing its usage entirely would negatively impact the speed with which an Intel device could complete this test. CHROMIUM: drm/i915/bdw: disable atomic We are uprevving the BDW chromebooks from kernel v3.14 to kernel v4.14. In v3.14 these systems did not support atomic, and as such did not support hardware overlays. With v4.14 we do support atomic, but it's a bit of work to get hardware overlays working. Until/unless this happens, stop advertising atomic support so userspace doesn't try and use hardware overlays. This keeps parity with the support that was offered with the older kernel.
